title: zazz script capabilities
description: What the zazz commands do for agents and people, and who may ask.

entities.name: Sandboxed scripts for agents and people
entities.description: Writing, testing, registering, signing and running small programs as WebAssembly (or, when trusted, native code) with the access their manifest asks for and their signer is granted.
entities.responsibility: Turns a script directory or .zazz file into a registered, tested script known by the hash of its bytes, runs it with JSON in and out for agents or as a command with flags for people, and decides what it may touch from its manifest, its signer's grants and the machine's policy.
access: Over the socket only a peer running as the daemon's own uid is served (server.rs check_peer); over MCP whoever started `zazzled mcp`.
MCP clients get new, test, pack, add, call, describe and ls only; signing, trust, install, run and rm are not offered there (mcptools.rs TOOLS).

Unsigned or untrusted scripts get no network and only their manifest's paths; a trusted signer's grants can add network hosts and native code and narrow paths, and the root-owned policy can switch network and native off or require tests (trust.rs policy, effective).

Trusting an authority writes root-owned /etc/zazzle/trust.d, which needs root, and on macOS asks the person to authenticate; files not owned by root there or in the policy are ignored (trust.rs root_owned).
Signing keys are the user's own 0600 files in ~/.zazzle/keys.

relatedViews.relationship: The operations through which the capability is reached.
